title: Base change of the Kummer coefficients
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], let $k$ be
algebraically closed, let $N\geq1$, and let $A$ be a finite
$\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z$-module which is free of finite rank (for
instance $A=A_{E,n}$ with $N=n\cdot v_\ell(\varpi_E)$ under the
hypothesis $e(E/\Ql)\mid n$ of [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]). For every
smooth separated curve $C$ over $k$ and every
integer $q\geq0$, the natural map

$$
H^q(C_{\Et},\mu_{\ell^N})\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A
\longrightarrow
H^q(C_{\Et},\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A)
$$

is an isomorphism. Here $A$ denotes the constant sheaf [def-kun-constant-sheaf] when it occurs in a sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and cohomology is that of underlying abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. More precisely, put $m=\ell^N$, $R=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$, and $F=\mu_m$, the kernel in [def-sc-kummer-sequence]. The map $\beta_A^q$ displayed above is characterized by
$$
\beta_A^q(x\otimes a)=H^q(i_a)(x),\qquad i_a:F\longrightarrow F\otimes_R A,\quad z\longmapsto z\otimes a.
$$
Compatibility with Kummer boundaries has the following precise meaning. Write $\partial^q:H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\to H^{q+1}(C_{\Et},F)$ for the boundary of the ordinary Kummer sequence. For any finite free abelian group $L$ and any isomorphism $L/mL\cong A$, take that Kummer sequence tensored over $\mathbf Z$ with $L$, which is a finite direct sum of the ordinary sequence. Identify its left term $F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L$ with $F\otimes_R A$. Its cohomology boundary, using $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L)\cong H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L$, descends to a map
$$
\partial_A^q:H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\longrightarrow H^{q+1}(C_{\Et},F\otimes_R A).
$$
This map is independent of the lift $L$ and satisfies, for every $u$ and $a$,
$$
\partial_A^q(u\otimes a)=\beta_A^{q+1}(\partial^q(u)\otimes a).
$$
Thus coefficient compatibility includes the usual units Kummer class in degree one. It does not require an $R$-module structure on $\mathbf G_m$.

proof.text: Work throughout on $C_{\Et}$ in abelian sheaves, retaining the $R$-action on $F$ and $F\otimes_R A$. By [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], this category has enough injectives and its section functor is additive and left exact. An ordinary injective resolution in nonnegative degrees is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so it is also a resolution allowed by the cohomology definition in the statement. Thus the cohomology functors here are precisely the right derived section functors of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] to that section functor. Each $H^q$ is therefore an additive functor, and connecting homomorphisms are natural for morphisms of short exact sequences. In particular $H^q(\sum f_j)=\sum H^q(f_j)$ and $H^q(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. Since $m\,\mathrm{id}_F=0$, also $m\,\mathrm{id}_{H^q(F)}=0$; the same holds for $F\otimes_R A$. The $R$-actions on their cohomology are induced by the scalar sheaf endomorphisms, so an $R$-linear sheaf map induces an $R$-linear map on cohomology.

proof.text: Choose a finite $R$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $A$, with coordinate functionals $\lambda_j:A\to R$; $r=0$ is allowed. Define $i_j:F\to F\otimes_R A$ by $z\mapsto z\otimes e_j$, and $p_j:F\otimes_R A\to F$ by $z\otimes a\mapsto\lambda_j(a)z$. These are sheaf morphisms: the displayed formulas are compatible with restriction and induce maps on the sheafified presheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By the locally constant function description of [def-kun-constant-sheaf], sections of $A$ have basis expansions with locally constant $R$-valued coordinates. Bilinearity gives $p_j i_h=\delta_{jh}\mathrm{id}_F$ and $\sum_j i_jp_j=\mathrm{id}_{F\otimes_R A}$. These identities hold on pure tensors locally and hence on the sheafification. They give explicit mutually inverse maps $F^{\oplus r}\leftrightarrows F\otimes_R A$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), definition of the sheafified tensor; explicit basis calculation supplied here.

proof.text:
For any $a\in A$ define $i_a(z)=z\otimes a$. The identities $i_{a+b}=i_a+i_b$ and $i_{ta}=i_a\circ(t\,\mathrm{id}_F)$, together with step 1, show that $(x,a)\mapsto H^q(i_a)(x)$ is $R$-bilinear: explicitly, $H^q(i_{ta})(x)=H^q(i_a)(t x)=t H^q(i_a)(x)$, and additivity gives the sum rule. Hence it kills the tensor balancing relation and induces the canonical map $\beta_A^q$. An explicit inverse is
$$y\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^r H^q(p_j)(y)\otimes e_j.$$
On $x\otimes a$ the composite is $\sum_j\lambda_j(a)x\otimes e_j=x\otimes a$, and on $y$ the other composite is $H^q(\sum_j i_jp_j)(y)=y$. This proves the asserted isomorphism in every degree. Its definition by the maps $i_a$ does not use a basis. For an $R$-linear map $h:A\to B$, $(\mathrm{id}_F\otimes h)i_a=i_{h(a)}$, so the same formula also proves naturality in the coefficient module.

proof.text:
The integer $m=\ell^N$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}k$, by the finite-field datum. The sequence $0\to F\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{m}\mathbf G_m\to0$ is short exact by [lem-sc-kummer-exact]. A lift exists: if $A\cong R^r$, take $L=\mathbf Z^r$ with its induced isomorphism $L/mL\cong A$. Now let $L$ be any finite free abelian lift with a specified isomorphism $L/mL\cong A$, and write $\bar l$ for the image of $l$ in $A$. Choose a basis $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $L$ and coordinate maps $b_j^*:L\to\mathbf Z$. Write abelian sheaf operations additively in the tensor formulas. For each of the abelian sheaves $G=F,\mathbf G_m$, define $J_j:G\to G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L$ by $g\mapsto g\otimes b_j$ and $P_j:G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L\to G$ by $g\otimes l\mapsto b_j^*(l)g$, using the tensor definition of step 2. Then $P_jJ_h=\delta_{jh}\mathrm{id}_G$ and $\sum_jJ_jP_j=\mathrm{id}_{G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L}$ by the basis expansion of $l$. These formulas identify the sequence tensored with $L$ with a finite direct sum of the ordinary Kummer sequence; its kernels are coordinatewise; a morphism out of the last direct sum that vanishes after the preceding map restricts to zero on each summand, because each ordinary last map is an epimorphism, and therefore is zero. Thus the last map is an epimorphism and the sequence is short exact. For $G=\mathbf G_m$, additivity from step 1 shows that the canonical map
$$
\alpha_L^q:H^q(G)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L\longrightarrow H^q(G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L),\qquad
u\otimes l\longmapsto H^q(g\mapsto g\otimes l)(u)
$$
has inverse $y\mapsto\sum_jH^q(P_j)(y)\otimes b_j$: the composites are $\sum_j b_j^*(l)u\otimes b_j=u\otimes l$ and $H^q(\sum_jJ_jP_j)(y)=y$. The left-term identification $F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L\cong F\otimes_R A$ sends $z\otimes l$ to $z\otimes\bar l$. Its inverse sends $z\otimes a$ locally to $z\otimes l$ for any lift $l$ of $a$; changing $l$ by $ml_0$ changes this by $z\otimes ml_0=mz\otimes l_0=0$, and this formula respects the $R$-balancing relation by taking integer representatives of its scalars. For each $l\in L$, the maps $g\mapsto g\otimes l$ on all three terms commute with the inclusion and multiplication by $m$, hence give a morphism from the ordinary Kummer sequence to the lifted sequence. Naturality of connecting maps from [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], with $\partial_L^q$ denoting the lifted boundary precomposed with $\alpha_L^q$ and followed by the left-term identification, gives
$$
\partial_L^q(u\otimes l)=H^{q+1}(i_{\bar l})(\partial^q(u))=\beta_A^{q+1}(\partial^q(u)\otimes\bar l).
$$

source.place: Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors), (4), naturality for the Kummer sequence; Kummer exactness supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: The formula in step 4 vanishes on $u\otimes ml$. The canonical quotient $(H^q(\mathbf G_m)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L)/\langle u\otimes ml\rangle$ is $H^q(\mathbf G_m)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}(L/mL)$: the quotient map kills every $u\otimes ml$, and maps from either quotient are exactly bilinear maps killing $(u,ml)$, by the universal property of the tensor product. Thus $\partial_L^q$ descends to $\partial_A^q$. The value on every pure tensor is $H^{q+1}(i_a)(\partial^q(u))=\beta_A^{q+1}(\partial^q(u)\otimes a)$. This expression depends only on $a$, not on $L$, its basis, or a lift of $a$; pure tensors generate the source, so it proves independence of all choices and the boundary compatibility in every degree. With $q=0$ it carries the ordinary Kummer class of a unit to its coefficient class. The proof also works for $A=0$, for the empty curve, and in degree zero.

lean.statement: theorem kummer_coefficient_base_change (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) [IsCurve f] [Smooth f] (A : ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N)))) [Module.Free (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N))) A] [Module.Finite (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N))) A] : ∃ (hm : IsUnit ((P.coefficients.l ^ N : ℕ) : Γ(C, ⊤))) (beta : ∀ q : ℕ, (Sheaf.H (C.rootsOfUnitySheaf (P.coefficients.l ^ N)) q ⊗[ ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N))] A) ≃ₗ[ ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod (P.coefficients.l ^ N))] Sheaf.H ((kummerAbelianTwist C (P.coefficients.l ^ N)).obj A) q), (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : Sheaf.H (C.rootsOfUnitySheaf (P.coefficients.l ^ N)) q) (a : A), beta q (x ⊗ₜ a) = Sheaf.H.map (kummerCoefficientInsertion C (P.coefficients.l ^ N) A a) q x) ∧ ∃ delta : ∀ q : ℕ, (Sheaf.H C.gmSheaf q ⊗[ℤ] A) →+ Sheaf.H ((kummerAbelianTwist C (P.coefficients.l ^ N)).obj A) (q + 1), (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : Sheaf.H C.gmSheaf q) (a : A), delta q (x ⊗ₜ[ℤ] a) = beta (q + 1) (Sheaf.H.δSucc (C.kummerSequence_shortExact (P.coefficients.l ^ N) hm) q x ⊗ₜ a)) ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, KummerIntegralLiftBoundary C (P.coefficients.l ^ N) q A (delta q)
